title: Separate PDO sign slopes gave no clear forecast gain in a 1981-2025 test
abstract: We tested separate persistence slopes for positive and negative Pacific Decadal Oscillation states. The reference model used current PDO, current Nino 3.4 and annual calendar terms. Expanding fits used only completed targets. In 540 one-month tests in 1981-2025, the sign term raised mean squared error from 0.314900 to 0.315242 index squared. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for error reduction was -0.320% to +0.146%. A six-month check gave a 0.154% reduction, with interval -0.996% to +1.209%. A 30-year fitting window gave higher error with the sign term. These results give no clear forecast gain under the main design. They do not reject physical asymmetry or explain the recent negative run. Revised surface indices, simple controls and uncertainty conditional on fitted forecasts limit the result. Code, source hashes, annual error aggregates, numerical checks and a figure are included. External source records are regenerated outside the publication.
